task_3.title: Fix VerifiedHTTPSConnection on Emscripten
task_3.description: urllib3 2.6.3 fixes Emscripten compatibility for callers that still use the legacy verified HTTPS connection name. After the Emscripten integration is injected, urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection should resolve to the patched Emscripten HTTPS connection implementation, and Emscripten connections should advertise the response wrapper expected by urllib3 response handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Emscripten users, including downstream libraries that still reference urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection, receive the patched urllib3 HTTPS connection behavior instead of an unsupported or unpatched connection path.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3.contrib.emscripten.inject_into_urllib3() is applied, urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection must be assigned to the same EmscriptenHTTPSConnection implementation used for urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection. EmscriptenHTTPConnection must also expose a response_class compatible with urllib3.response.BaseHTTPResponse via the Emscripten response wrapper.
expectation.conceptual: Code running in an Emscripten environment should be able to use both the current HTTPS connection API and the older verified HTTPS connection alias, with responses behaving like normal urllib3 HTTP responses.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing Emscripten injection behavior for HTTPConnection, HTTPSConnection, HTTPConnectionPool.ConnectionCls, and HTTPSConnectionPool.ConnectionCls. Do not change the public semantics of non-Emscripten connection classes or remove the legacy VerifiedHTTPSConnection name.
constraints.conceptual: The compatibility fix should be limited to making the Emscripten integration work for legacy and current callers without regressing existing urllib3 connection behavior.

behavior: After Emscripten injection, urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection resolves to EmscriptenHTTPSConnection.
Callers that instantiate VerifiedHTTPSConnection in an Emscripten runtime use the patched Emscripten HTTPS transport.
EmscriptenHTTPConnection exposes a response_class pointing to the Emscripten HTTP response wrapper.
Responses obtained through the Emscripten connection path remain compatible with urllib3.response.BaseHTTPResponse expectations.
Existing Emscripten replacements for HTTPConnection, HTTPSConnection, HTTPConnectionPool.ConnectionCls, and HTTPSConnectionPool.ConnectionCls remain active.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Emscripten runtime where urllib3.contrib.emscripten.inject_into_urllib3() has been called, when code reads urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection, then it should receive the Emscripten HTTPS connection class.

When a downstream library constructs urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection after Emscripten injection, it should use the patched Emscripten HTTPS behavior rather than the standard HTTPS connection implementation.
When an Emscripten connection returns an HTTP response, the response should satisfy urllib3's BaseHTTPResponse-compatible behavior.
When Emscripten injection is used, existing patched HTTP and HTTPS connection pool class mappings should continue to work as before.

task_2.title: Cap excessive Retry-After delays
task_2.description: Retry-After values from remote servers are now bounded so that extremely large delay values cannot cause overflow errors or impractically long sleeps. The default maximum delay is six hours, and callers can configure a different maximum through the Retry API.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 handles excessively large Retry-After header values safely by capping the effective retry delay, while allowing applications to configure the maximum permitted Retry-After delay.

expectation.grounded: Retry.DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER_MAX should expose the default cap of 21600 seconds. Retry should accept a retry_after_max parameter, preserve it when creating derived Retry instances, and have Retry.parse_retry_after return no more than that configured maximum for any parsed Retry-After delay. Retry.sleep_for_retry should therefore never sleep longer than the configured Retry-After maximum.
expectation.conceptual: When a server asks a client to wait for an excessive amount of time before retrying, the client should treat that request as a bounded delay rather than failing with an overflow or waiting for an unreasonable duration. Applications should be able to lower or raise that bound according to their retry policy.

constraints.grounded: Existing Retry behavior outside Retry-After delay bounding must remain unchanged, including validation of invalid Retry-After header values, normalization of past or negative computed delays to zero, backoff_max behavior for exponential backoff, and existing retry/redirect/status configuration semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be limited to bounding server-provided retry delays and must not alter unrelated retry decisions, redirect handling, status handling, or client-side exponential backoff behavior.

behavior: Retry exposes a default maximum Retry-After delay of six hours, represented as 21600 seconds.
Retry instances can be configured with a retry_after_max value that controls the largest Retry-After delay they will honor.
Parsed Retry-After delays greater than the configured maximum are returned as the configured maximum instead of the original excessive value.
Parsed Retry-After delays at or below the configured maximum are returned according to the existing parsing semantics.
Derived Retry instances retain the same retry_after_max setting as the instance they were created from.
Retry.sleep_for_retry observes the capped value because it uses the parsed Retry-After delay.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Retry instance with default configuration, when a Retry-After header represents more than six hours of delay, it should be treated as a six-hour delay.
Given a Retry instance with a custom retry_after_max, when a Retry-After header represents a delay greater than that custom maximum, it should be treated as the custom maximum.
When a Retry-After header represents a delay less than or equal to the configured maximum, it should be honored using the existing parsing behavior.
When a Retry instance creates a derived Retry object during retry processing, the configured Retry-After maximum should continue to apply to the derived object.
When retry sleep behavior is driven by Retry-After, it should use the bounded delay and should not attempt to sleep for an unbounded server-provided value.

task_1.title: Preserve streaming decompression safeguards across redirects
task_1.description: The update fixes a high-severity security issue in which urllib3's streaming API could bypass decompression-bomb protections when following HTTP redirects. Redirect response cleanup now avoids initiating content decoding solely to drain an unread response body, while still allowing already-started decoding to continue consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that following HTTP redirects in streaming response workflows preserves decompression-bomb safeguards and does not unnecessarily decode compressed redirect response bodies.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3 follows redirects and drains an intermediate HTTPResponse, the drain path must not cause HTTPResponse.read() to start content decoding for an unread compressed redirect body unless decoding for that response has already begun. This applies to streaming API usage and to redirect responses carrying a compressed content encoding.
expectation.conceptual: Redirect handling should safely discard intermediate response bodies without unexpectedly decompressing them in streaming mode. Users who opt into streaming should retain the same protection against oversized decompressed payloads when redirects are followed as they have for non-redirected responses.

constraints.grounded: Do not change normal redirect following semantics, final response status handling, connection release behavior, or the ability to continue decoding a response whose content decoding has already been initiated. Existing HTTPResponse.read() behavior with explicit decoding choices should remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to preserving safe streaming behavior during redirects and should not alter ordinary request results, redirect resolution, or legitimate response decoding behavior.

behavior: Draining an unread intermediate redirect response no longer starts decompression merely because the response advertises a compressed content encoding.
If content decoding for a response has already begun before draining, draining continues consistently with that decoded state.
Streaming requests that follow redirects preserve decompression-bomb safeguards instead of bypassing them through redirect cleanup.
Compressed redirect responses can still be followed and their connections can still be drained or released without forcing decoder work when the caller has not requested decoded content.
acceptance_criteria: Given a streaming request that follows one or more redirects, when an intermediate redirect response includes a compressed body, then redirect handling should not initiate decompression solely to drain that intermediate body.
Given an HTTPResponse whose content decoding has already started, when the response is drained, then draining should remain consistent with the already-started decoded state.

When redirects are followed in streaming mode, the final response should still be returned according to normal redirect behavior while preserving decompression-bomb protections for intermediate compressed responses.
When redirect responses do not require decoding during cleanup, connection draining and reuse behavior should continue without exposing users to unnecessary decompression work.
